title: Marcos to uphold national interest while seeking better trade deals with China
summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Wednesday committed to upholding national interest even as he intends to engage with China “constructively” to expand trade and investment amid the APEC…

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Wednesday committed to upholding national interest even as he intends to engage with China “constructively” to expand trade and investment amid the APEC Summit.
Marcos is set to fly to Shenzhen, China Wednesday afternoon to participate in the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting (AELM).
In his departure message, Marcos said that his attendance at the AELM and other related activities was upon the invitation of Chinese President Xi Jinping.

“We will engage China constructively on expanding trade, investment, and people-to-people exchanges that benefit our peoples, even as we remain steadfast in upholding our national interest,” the President said.
“Our message is clear—the Philippines is open for business. Invest in the Filipino,” he added.

As chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) for 2026, Marcos said he will bring to APEC the gains of the country’s chairship, including the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA)—-the world's first region-wide digital economy agreement.
“ASEAN and APEC share the same goal—an open, connected, and inclusive region. Real growth and lasting prosperity come when we break down barriers and work together,” he said.
On the sidelines of the summit, Marcos said he also plans to meet fellow leaders and engage with the business community to deepen trade ties and attract investment for the Philippines.

He also expressed commitment to opening new markets for Filipino products and talent, accelerating digital transformation, and building partnerships that bring investment and quality jobs to the country’s economy.
“APEC is a platform for dialogue and discussion, but what matters most is what our conversations bring home: more jobs, better access to healthcare, and an economy ready for the future,” Marcos said.

“I am confident that our participation in Shenzhen will produce concrete outcomes that bring us closer to that goal. This is our promise—real change for every Filipino today and for the generations to come,” he added. —AOL, GMA News
